chart.reason: The dataset contains rich multi-year trends, group comparisons, and ranked distributions; charts are the primary medium for the analytical spine.

image.reason: Five conceptual images break analytical density and carry the warm-shelter tone — silhouettes and abstractions are used so no live or distressing animal imagery appears.

video.reason: No specific event, motion, or transformation is central to the story. The strongest moments are quantitative and a chart or interactive carries them better than a 5-second clip.

audio.reason: The dataset has no sonic dimension. Recent blog templates have over-relied on click-to-play tone cards; skipping audio is the data-driven, anti-sameness choice.

interactive_or_map.reason: The save-rate-vs-90% benchmark gap and the ZIP-level intake distribution both reward exploration. A guess-first reveal on the asterisk effect rewards the surprise.

des_teaser.label: Teaser hero — the empty intake counter

content.prompt: Cinematic editorial photograph of an empty animal shelter intake counter at warm dawn light, a single ID-tag clipboard with a small star drawn in pencil sitting on a worn wooden surface, soft amber and golden hour lighting from a window off-screen, shallow depth of field, no animals visible, no text on the page, restrained mood, photographic, 16:9

des_teaser.brief: Full-bleed warm photograph used behind the headline. Mood: quiet front-desk before the day's intake. The pencilled star on the clipboard is the single visual hint of the asterisk theme; do not overlay any text on the image inside the frame.
des_teaser.rationale: A still image creates the right contemplative tone for an open-admission-shelter story. Animals as abstractions/silhouettes (and the pencil star as metaphor) avoid distressing imagery.

des_01.label: Hook stat callouts — three categories
des_01.brief: Three large stat callouts arranged as a horizontal triplet just under the headline. Each shows the percentage in 64px serif, a one-line label, and a small total. Cards are paper-tan with warm rules.
des_01.rationale: The three-bucket split is the editorial spine — it deserves headline weight before the first chart.

des_02.label: Hook chart — owner-named vs staff-named outcomes

highlight.annotation: Owner-named animals go home 41.3% of the time

content.interaction: hover bar reveals exact pct and absolute n

des_02.brief: Three rows (owner_named / staff_named / blank), each row has three bars: return-to-owner pct, adoption pct, save pct. The 41.3% RTO bar for owner_named is the visual centrepiece — annotate it. The 0.8% bars for staff_named and blank should be visibly small to the same scale, making the contrast self-evident.
des_02.rationale: The grouped bar is the cleanest way to show the central tension — that the asterisk does not change save rate but does change pathway.

des_03.label: Three-categories conceptual image

content.prompt: Warm conceptual illustration of three abstract animal silhouettes side by side under soft golden light: one cat silhouette filled with a cream tag-shape, one dog silhouette filled with a soft star-shape, one third silhouette empty/hollow showing only outline. Editorial flat illustration style, cream and dusty rose and amber palette, soft paper texture, no text, no faces, calm and tender mood, 16:9

des_03.brief: Inline 16:9 illustration that visually anchors the three-bucket split (tag, star, hollow). Used as a closing visual for the hook section before the reader scrolls into the species mix.
des_03.rationale: Restates the three categories as a visual metaphor without showing any specific animal — keeps tone gentle and abstract.

des_04.label: Species mix donut + long tail

content.interaction: hover shows exact count and pct

des_04.brief: Single horizontal bar chart with 10 species sorted by count desc. Cat and dog use the darker accent_warm tone, the rest use accent_amber. Each bar has its percentage right-aligned at the end. The chart's caption notes 'including 3 amphibians'.
des_04.rationale: A bar chart is more honest for very long-tailed distributions than a donut; the long tail (livestock 10, amphibian 3) is part of the surprise.

des_05.label: Species ensemble illustration

content.prompt: Editorial flat illustration: a soft circular composition showing many small abstract silhouettes of different shelter animals arranged like a wheel — cat, dog, rabbit, parrot, lizard, hawk, guinea pig, opossum — all in muted cream, warm rose, dusty amber, sage green, terracotta. Paper-cut texture, calm, no text, no detailed faces, conceptual ensemble illustration, 16:9

des_05.brief: Square-ish illustration showing the species mix as silhouettes in a wheel. Sits to the right of the species bar chart, balancing the analytical chart with a warm visual.
des_05.rationale: The variety of species is the section's emotional point; an illustration carries it more directly than another stat.

des_06.label: Quarterly intake area chart with annotations

style.vertical_gridline_at_2019Q2: subtle dashed for Compassion Saves vote

des_06.brief: Smooth filled-area chart over 32 quarters. Three labelled callouts: lockdown start, trough, 2024 peak. A subtle dashed vertical line at 2019Q2 marks the Compassion Saves council vote (May 2019), labelled 'Compassion Saves' but kept visually quiet.
des_06.rationale: Quarterly resolution shows the V more cleanly than the annual bar chart and lets us mark the policy date without overstating causation.

des_07.label: Annual intake mini-bars (small-multiple)
des_07.brief: Small annual bar chart inset that complements the quarterly area chart — eight bars, 2017 to 2024, with the 2021 bar highlighted in a darker tone.
des_07.rationale: A second compact view confirms the V at the annual scale and gives the reader a reference grid for the quarterly chart above.

des_08.label: Kitten season radial / line
des_08.brief: Two-line chart over 12 months. The kitten line is bright terracotta and filled under; the all-intakes line is dusty plum. May is annotated with the 901 number and 11x callout. The shape mimics seasonal rainfall, which is the point.
des_08.rationale: Seasonality reads naturally as a curve; the dual line lets the kitten spike sit inside the broader monthly curve so readers see both.

des_09.label: Kitten season conceptual image

content.prompt: Editorial conceptual illustration: a soft cream-colored shoebox set on warm wooden surface, lined with a thin folded blanket, holding tiny abstract kitten silhouettes barely visible. Soft golden-hour window light from upper left. Warm rose and amber palette, paper-cut texture, gentle, calm, no text, no detailed faces, evocative of fostered neonatal kittens during kitten season, 16:9

des_09.brief: Inline atmospheric image accompanying the seasonality chart. Conceptual not literal — the foster-shoebox is a visual shorthand for the operational reality without showing real kittens.
des_09.rationale: Avoids distressing imagery while still conveying the foster-program scale that the data forces.

des_10.label: Save rate vs 90% benchmark — interactive line

content.initial_state: Line chart of cat+dog save rate by year (2017-2024) with the horizontal 90% no-kill benchmark drawn as a dashed line. Years 2017-2018 sit visibly below; 2020 sits above; 2024 sits between.
content.trigger: Reader clicks year-buttons (2017, 2019, 2020, 2024) below the chart
content.transition: Selected year's data flips on a card next to the chart: total cats+dogs out, live, % live. The point on the chart pulses.
content.payoff: Reader sees that 2024's record adoptions did not push the rate above the line, while 2020's collapse-in-intake did.

des_10.brief: A line chart with the 90% benchmark as a dashed horizontal line. Below the chart, four year-buttons act as a step navigator. Clicking a year fills a small detail card to the chart's right with that year's total/live/save_pct. The annotation 'after Compassion Saves' sits between 2018 and 2019 on the line, and the prose around the chart explicitly says 'coincides with' to honour caveat ana_caveat_06.
des_10.rationale: Interactive year selection rewards readers for engaging with the central tension (record adoptions, flat rate) rather than passing past a single chart.

des_11.label: Outcome composition stacked bars by year

content.interaction: toggle between absolute counts and 100% normalized; hover gives bucket+year+count+pct

des_11.brief: 8 yearly stacks (2017-2024). Adoption (warm cream), rescue/transfer (sage), return-to-owner (amber), TNR/wildlife (dusty plum), euthanasia (terracotta), died/disposal (deep cocoa). A toggle lets the reader switch between absolute counts and 100% normalised view — both are revealing in different ways.
des_11.rationale: Stacked-bars carry composition over time efficiently; the toggle resolves the absolute-vs-percentage tension that is the centrepiece argument.

des_12.label: Save rate by species — slope from 90% line
des_12.brief: Horizontal lollipop chart, 9 species sorted by save_pct desc. A vertical dashed line at 90% labelled as the no-kill benchmark. Dogs/reptiles/guinea pigs sit right of the line; cats sit just left; wild sits far left with an explanatory annotation. Sample-size badges (n) appear next to each species name.
des_12.rationale: Lollipops emphasize the position relative to the benchmark line better than bars; sorting reveals an unexpected order (guinea pigs top, dogs second).

des_13.label: Outcome by species heatmap
des_13.brief: 6 rows (dog, cat, bird, wild, rabbit, guinea pig) by 7 columns (adoption, return-to-owner, rescue, transfer, euthanasia, TNR/wild-release, died/disposal). Color = percentage within row. Strong cells get their pct rendered in white text.
des_13.rationale: A heatmap conveys the species-specific outcome divergence in one block — much faster than six separate bar charts.

des_14.label: Triage condition save rate — gradient bar
des_14.brief: 15 horizontal bars sorted desc by save_pct, color graded warm-to-cool by save_pct. Vertical 90% reference line. The 'normal' bar tops the chart; 'ill severe' and 'injured severe' anchor the bottom.
des_14.rationale: Sorting and the 90% line communicate the magnitude of the medical-tail problem at a glance, supporting the section's argument that triage drives the headline rate.

des_15.label: Owner surrender reasons bar

content.interaction: hover gives count and pct of total surrenders

des_15.brief: 18 bars, sorted desc. Top four bars (owner problem, move, landlord, cost) are accent_warm; the rest are accent_amber. A bracket annotation visually groups the top four with the '~51%' tag. A small caption notes 'new baby — 13' to make the surprise visible.
des_15.rationale: The hierarchy of housing/cost reasons is the section's argument; emphasising the top four directly communicates that.

des_16.label: Length of stay by outcome — dot plot
des_16.brief: Dot plot, x = median LOS in days, y = outcome bucket (8 categories), dot size = count. Adoption is the rightmost large dot (slow path); return-to-owner is the leftmost (fastest); euthanasia at 0 days reads as immediate.
des_16.rationale: The shape of the dataset's exit-pace lives at the median; a dot plot with size for sample reveals both axis quickly.

des_17.label: Intake by ZIP — interactive map

content.initial_state: Leaflet map centred on Long Beach (33.78N, -118.14W) at zoom 12. Each top ZIP from ana_21 shown as a labelled circle marker with radius proportional to intake count. The shelter's own location is marked with a small star icon and a tooltip noting the address-default artefact (ana_23 / 560 intakes).
content.transition: Tooltip shows ZIP + intake count + percent of total
content.payoff: Reader sees that intake is concentrated in 90805 / 90813 / 90806, North and Central Long Beach, with the shelter site as an obvious self-bin.

des_17.brief: A real interactive Leaflet map with one circle marker per top-12 ZIP, sized by intake count, plus a star icon at 33.810/-118.085 (the shelter) with a hover tooltip explaining the 560-intake artefact. OpenStreetMap tiles. Map height 420px.
des_17.rationale: A real map is more honest than a faux choropleth and lets the reader explore — the geography is genuine here, not decoration.

des_18.label: Top names — paired list

highlight.name: Luna
highlight.annotation: the only top-name across both species

des_18.brief: Two-column 'face-off' chart. Left column: dog top-8, sorted desc. Right column: cat top-8. Bars meet at the center axis. Luna's name is highlighted on both sides with a small connecting line/annotation.
des_18.rationale: The species-naming divergence reads instantly in a face-off, and Luna's dual presence becomes a small reveal.

des_19.label: Naming fingerprint by intake type

style.palette: warm/amber/dusk for the three name buckets

des_19.brief: 8 horizontal stacked bars (one per intake_type) totalling 100%, segments colored by name status. Owner surrender's bar is mostly warm. Wildlife's is almost all dusk. TNR's is mostly amber. The visual 'fingerprint' of each intake type is unmistakable.
des_19.rationale: 100%-stacked is the right form for proportions; sorting by intake_type matches editorial reading order.

des_20.label: Closing image — empty crate

content.prompt: Editorial conceptual illustration: a calm scene of an open dog crate door against an empty room, with a leash lying coiled on a worn wood floor and a single sunlit collar nearby. Soft warm tones, cream wall, dusty amber light, paper-cut illustration style, no text, no faces, no animals visible, gentle empty-room mood, 16:9

des_20.brief: Quiet, empty-room illustration to close the piece. The open crate door reads as both 'someone went home' and 'the kennel is ready for the next intake', matching the tension in the closing prose.
des_20.rationale: The closing argument is two simultaneously-true facts; an open-empty image holds the ambiguity better than a celebratory or sad one.

page_rhythm.text_visual_pattern: stat-callout hook → image → analytic chart → atmospheric image → interactive turn → analytic supporting charts → map → close on image
page_rhythm.anti_sameness_notes: No audio card. No card-deck pattern. No video. Map is real Leaflet not a fake choropleth. Charts span seven distinct types (lollipop, heatmap, dual-line, area, stacked-bar with toggle, paired-bar, dot-plot) so the page does not feel like a dashboard. Imagery is conceptual and abstract — silhouettes and objects, never photographic animals — which honours the ethical brief about avoiding distressing shelter imagery.
page_rhythm.typography_notes: Headline serif, body sans. Stat callouts at ~64-72px. Large pull quote allowed once around edt_05's turn. Section dividers are a thin warm-tan rule (#D9CDB8). Body line-height 1.6. Max content width ~720px for prose; charts and the map allowed to expand to ~960px.
